'''Caleb Sylvester Swanigan''' (April 18, 1997 – June 20, 2022) was an American professional [[basketball]] player in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]].<ref name="Fox25">{{cite news |last=Organ |first=Aaron |title=Caleb Swanigan, former Purdue star and NBA player, dead at 25 |url=https://fox59.com/news/caleb-swanigan-former-purdue-star-dead-at-25/ |access-date=June 21, 2022 |work=Fox 59 |date=June 21, 2022 |archive-date=August 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829223452/https://fox59.com/news/caleb-swanigan-former-purdue-star-dead-at-25/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was ranked among the top prep players in the national class of 2015 by [[Rivals.com]], [[Scout.com]] and [[ESPN]]. He completed his senior season in the 2014–15 academic year for [[Homestead High School (Indiana)|Homestead High School]] in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], who went on to win the first state championship in the school's history. Swanigan was named [[Indiana]]'s [[Mr. Basketball]] and a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]].

Swanigan originally committed to [[Michigan State University]], but later decommitted and committed to [[Purdue University]]. He was named [[Big Ten]] Freshman of the Week three times, a record at Purdue. He was also named to the Big Ten All-Freshman Team and also received a National Freshman of the Week award. Swanigan finished the season with 10.2 points per game and 8.3 rebounds per game.

During his sophomore year, Swanigan was named the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] and first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]], and was a unanimous first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was a finalist for the 2017 [[Karl Malone Award]], given to the nation's top [[power forward]]. He was selected 26th overall in the first round of the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="nytimes_draft">{{cite news |last1=Hoffman |first1=Benjamin |last2=Tracy |first2=Marc |name-list-style=and |date=June 22, 2017 |title=N.B.A. Draft: Analysis of Every Pick and Trade in Round 1 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/22/sports/nba-draft.html |access-date=June 24, 2017 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref> Over his three-year NBA career, Swanigan had two stints with the Trail Blazers; he also played for the [[Sacramento Kings]].

==Early life==
Swanigan grew up in an unstable home due to his father, Carl Swanigan Sr., who had a [[crack cocaine]] addiction. Swanigan's mother, Tanya, had six children. Swanigan moved between [[Utah]] and [[Indianapolis]] during his youth, spending time in homeless shelters.<ref name=Medcalf>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18523734 |title=Purdue's Caleb Swanigan has changed his body and his life |first=Myron |last=Medcalf |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 24, 2017 |access-date=February 17, 2023}}</ref>

Swanigan inherited two key features from his biological father—height and a tendency to obesity. The elder Swanigan, who died in 2014 from complications from [[Diabetes mellitus|diabetes]], was {{height|ft=6|in=8}} and weighed nearly {{convert|500|lb}} at his death. By the time Swanigan was entering eighth grade, he was {{height|ft=6|in=2}} and {{convert|360|lb}}.<ref name=Medcalf/> His father had many brushes with the law, battled drug addiction for most of his adult life, and physically assaulted his wife. According to a story in [[Bleacher Report]], Swanigan was accidentally dropped by his mother as an infant, leaving a bruise on his face; this incident led her to move with her children to [[Salt Lake City]]. For the next decade, the family bounced between Indianapolis and Utah; he recalled that he lived in five different homeless shelters and attended 13 different schools by the time he was 13.<ref name=Medcalf/>

When his mother decided to move the family to [[Houston]], his older brother Carl Jr., concerned that Caleb would keep gaining weight if he moved with his mother, called his former [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball coach, [[Roosevelt Barnes (American football)|Roosevelt Barnes]], a former three-sport star at Purdue who played on the school's [[1980 NCAA Division I basketball tournament|1980 Final Four]] [[1979–80 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|team]] and now a successful [[sports agent]]. Barnes, living in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], agreed to take Caleb in if he could [[adopt]] him and raise him as his own son. Barnes adopted Swanigan prior to his 8th-grade year. Barnes addressed Swanigan's eating habits and, after receiving clearance from a cardiologist, began putting him through workouts similar to those Barnes himself went through in college. By the time Swanigan finished high school, he had slimmed down to {{convert|260|lb}}.<ref name=Medcalf/>

==High school career==
[[File:20150401 MCDAAG Caleb Swanigan rebounds in front of Diamond Stone (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Swanigan in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] in 2015]]
In the fall of 2011, Swanigan attended a basketball camp led by NBA former coach [[John Lucas II|John Lucas]] after Roosevelt Barnes convinced Lucas to let him into the invite-only camp in [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]].<ref name="br">{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2580780-homelessness-heartache-and-hoops-caleb-swanigans-rough-road-to-purdue|title=Homelessness, Heartache and Hoops: Caleb Swanigan's Rough Road to Purdue|last=King|first=Jason|website=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=October 21, 2015}}</ref> When it came to selecting his high school, Swanigan's guardian Barnes said, "When he chose his high school, his high school had never really done much in the tournament, and his goal was to win a state championship at a school where that had never been done before."<ref name="jc"/> Swanigan attended [[Homestead High School (Indiana)|Homestead High School]] and wore the same number as Barnes, number 44.<ref name="br"/>

As a senior, he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] and led Homestead to its first-ever state title. He was ranked as a top-20 national prospect in his class.<ref name="indystar">{{cite news|last=Neddenriep|first=Kyle|title=Caleb Swanigan wants to bring a title to Purdue|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/purdue/2015/05/19/mr-basketball-caleb-swanigan-commits-to-purdue/27578647/|access-date=June 27, 2015|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=May 20, 2015}}</ref> He was named a [[McDonald's All-American]].<ref name=EWru>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12243846 |title=East, West rosters unveiled|access-date=February 17, 2023|date=January 28, 2015|publisher=ESPN|last=Borzello|first=Jeff}}</ref> Swanigan averaged 22.6 points and 13.7 rebounds as a senior.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Johnson|first=Chris|title=Breaking down college basketball's top 25 recruits for 2015: Nos. 20–16|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/07/17/top-25-recruits-caleb-swanigan-jalen-brunson-jalen-adams|access-date=July 22, 2015|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=July 21, 2015}}</ref> Academically, Swanigan maintained a 3.1 [[GPA]] and graduated in three years instead of the usual four.<ref name="usa"/>

Swanigan finished his career at Homestead with records for career points (1,649) and rebounds (1,048), as well as the single-season points (704) and rebounding records (424).<ref name="indystar"/> He was also second all time for career blocks (106) and assists (204).<ref name="purdue"/>

==National team career==
Swanigan qualified for the 2014 U17 World Championship Team, beating out twenty other players vying for a spot to make the 12-man squad.<ref name="wane">{{cite web|url=http://wane.com/2014/07/29/homesteads-swanigan-named-to-u17-national-team/|title=Homestead's Swanigan named to U17 national team|website=wane.com|access-date=March 21, 2017|date=July 29, 2014|archive-date=March 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321171353/http://wane.com/2014/07/29/homesteads-swanigan-named-to-u17-national-team/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Swanigan played in the U17 World Championship Game. The team finished with a 7–0 record and earned a gold medal in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, extending the USA's total record at the U17 World Championship Game to 23–0.<ref name="wane"/> He finished the series with 8.0 points per game and 5.7 rebounds per game,<ref name="usa"/> and was the most efficient player on the U17 team, with a 69.6 shooting percentage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2152838-top-2015-recruit-caleb-swanigan-an-old-school-big-ready-to-bang-with-cbbs-best|title=Top 2015 Recruit Caleb Swanigan an Old-School Big Ready to Bang with CBB's Best|access-date=March 20, 2017|website=Bleacher Report|last=Moore|first=C.J.|date=August 31, 2014}}</ref>

Before starting his freshman season at Purdue, on June 18, 2015, Swanigan was announced as a member of the 12-man 2015 USA Basketball Men's U19 World Championship Team for the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] that won a gold medal in Heraklion, Crete.<ref name="usab">{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/06/usa-mens-u19-team-named.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618150413/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/06/usa-mens-u19-team-named.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 18, 2015|title=USA Basketball 2015 Men's U19 World Championship Team Named|access-date=July 2, 2015|date=June 18, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> On making the team, Swanigan said, "I always set goals for myself. I set goals for this spring. One of my goals is to make this team to end my high school career."<ref name="usab"/> To prepare for the games, Swanigan played in the Nike Hoop Summit, the McDonald's All American Game, and the Jordan Brand Classic. Swanigan did not take part in the Indiana-Kentucky All Star Game so he could attend the U19 training camp.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.journalgazette.net/sports/high-schools/Swanigan-selected-to-U19-USA-Basketball-team-7248017|title=Swanigan selected to U19 USA Basketball team|website=Journal Gazette|date=June 18, 2015|access-date=March 21, 2017|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322204659/http://www.journalgazette.net/sports/high-schools/Swanigan-selected-to-U19-USA-Basketball-team-7248017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was one of five players returning from the gold medal-winning U17 squad. Swanigan's teammate [[Vincent Edwards (basketball)|Vince Edwards]] was also in the running to make the team, but was cut at the round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/061715aab.html|title=Swanigan Selected to Represent Team USA at U19 World Championship|date=June 17, 2015|access-date=March 21, 2017|publisher=Purdue Sports|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130013610/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/061715aab.html|archive-date=January 30, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The team finished 7–0, and Swanigan averaged 6.1 points and 4.4 rebounds per game.<ref name="usa">{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/swanigan-caleb.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623013833/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/swanigan-caleb.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 23, 2015|title=Caleb Swanigan|access-date=March 19, 2017|website=USA Basketball}}</ref>

==College career==

===Recruiting===
Swanigan had several teams recruit him and offer scholarships; [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Cal]] and [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] were among the schools that gave Swanigan an offer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/185326/caleb-swanigan|title=Caleb Swanigan Recruiting|access-date=March 19, 2016|website=ESPN}}</ref> Caleb Swanigan verbally committed to [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] on April 10, 2015, but decommitted on May 7.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12664698 |title=Caleb Swanigan, No. 8 in ESPN 100, commits to Michigan St.|access-date=February 17, 2023|date=April 10, 2015|publisher=ESPN|last=Borzello|first=Jeff}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12842567 |title=Sources: Caleb Swanigan decommits from Michigan State Spartans|access-date=February 17, 2023|date=May 7, 2015|publisher=ESPN|last=Goodman|first=Jeff}}</ref> He said, "I just felt like it was better basketball-wise for me."<ref name="Medcalf" /> Similar to his high school decision, Roosevelt Barnes said, "He wants to win a national championship and said he wants to do it in the state of Indiana and wanted to do it at a place he's never done it before."<ref name="jc" /> Some people believe Barnes had ulterior motives in adopting Swanigan, to which Barnes said, "Maybe if I wanted to develop the next [[Competitive eating|hot dog-eating]] champion, the next [[Joey Chestnut]], people would have a legitimate gripe." Swanigan had not consulted Barnes before he committed to Michigan State, and some believe that since Barnes played sports at Purdue he was a major influence in Swanigan decommitting from Michigan State. Barnes said that was not the reason Swanigan switched, and the primary reason for Swanigan choosing Purdue was the presence of two centers that were taller than 7 feet, [[Isaac Haas]] and [[A. J. Hammons]], which allowed Swanigan to play the [[Power forward|4 spot]].<ref name="br"/>

He decided to stay in-state and chose [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] on May 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/12913332/ |title=Caleb Swanigan commits to Purdue|access-date=February 17, 2023|date=May 19, 2015|publisher=ESPN|last=Borzello|first=Jeff}}</ref> Swanigan announced his decision by tweeting "#BoilerUp". Swanigan was Purdue's first Indiana's Mr. Basketball recruit since [[Glenn Robinson]] in 1991, and was the first [[McDonald's All-American]] for Purdue since 1996.<ref name="jc">{{cite web|url=http://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2015/05/19/purdue-mens-basketball-caleb-swanigan-commitment/27577873/|title=Mr. Basketball Caleb Swanigan commits to Purdue|website=Lafayette Journal and Courier|date=May 19, 2015|last=Baird|first=Nathan|access-date=April 8, 2017}}</ref> Swanigan joined Ryan Cline and Grant Weatherford in Purdue's 2015 recruiting class.<ref name="indystar"/>

===2015–16 season===
Swanigan chose to major in general education/educational studies.<ref name="purdue"/> Swanigan chose the number 50 to honor his father who had died at 50 years old.<ref name="br"/> Swanigan started every game his freshman year. His highest-scoring game was in a win against Wisconsin in Purdue's last regular-season game, where he scored 27 points and missed only one shot from the field. He scored six points and grabbed 10 rebounds in #4 Purdue's loss to #13 [[2015–16 Little Rock Trojans men's basketball team|Arkansas–Little Rock]] in the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], and did not play at all during the overtime period.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/caleb-swanigan-1/gamelog/2016|title=Caleb Swanigan 2015–16 Game Log|access-date=March 20, 2017|website=Sports Reference}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jconline.com/story/sports/blogs/nathan-baird/2016/03/18/notebook-trojans-forced-purdue-go-small/81956618/|title=Little Rock forced Purdue to go small|last=Baird|first=Nathan|website=Lafayette Journal and Courier|access-date=March 21, 2017|date=March 18, 2016}}</ref>

After his freshman season, Swanigan was one out of 162 underclassmen to enter their names for the [[2016 NBA draft]]. However, despite being one of 63 invitees for the [[NBA draft combine]] that year, he ultimately decided to return to college on May 25, which was also the new date set for players to withdraw their names from the draft and try again for another year. An NBA scout said, "I think he has a chance if he can improve his jump shot and help defense. Big-time rebounder, works hard on his own. He's still more undersized [[Center (basketball)|center]] than [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], though."<ref name="Medcalf"/>

Swanigan set several records as a freshman. He was ranked as a top-10 freshman nationally. He set Purdue program records for most rebounds by a freshman (282), games started (34), double-doubles (8) and rebounds per game (8.3).<ref name="purdue"/> He was also the first major-college player in 25 years that had 600 points, 400 rebounds and 100 assists in a season.<ref name="p2"/>

===2016–17 season===
Similar to his freshman year, Swanigan started every game as a sophomore. Swanigan set his personal record for points against Norfolk State with 32, while shooting 83% from the field. Swanigan also managed to grab 20 rebounds, making it one of his four games with at least 20 points and 20 rebounds that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/caleb-swanigan-1/gamelog/2017|title=Caleb Swanigan 2016–17 Game Log|website=Sports Reference|access-date=March 20, 2017}}</ref>

As of March 6, 2017, Swanigan was second in the nation in rebounds per game (12.6) and led the nation in double doubles (25) for the 2016–17 season. He was rated first in CBS National Player of the Year voting.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-player-of-the-year-rankings-caleb-swanigan-jumps-to-no-1/|website=CBS Sports|last=Parrish|first=Gary|date=February 21, 2017|title=College Basketball Player of the Year rankings: Caleb Swanigan jumps to No. 1|access-date=March 20, 2017}}</ref> In his sophomore season, Swanigan broke several Purdue records, including rebounds in a season, double-doubles in a season, and an NCAA record with four 20–20 performances. Purdue finished as the regular season Big Ten Champions, but were knocked out in the quarterfinals of the Big Ten Tournament by Michigan, the eventual tournament champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030217aaa.html|website=B1G|title=Purdue Men's Basketball Clinches Outright Big Ten Championship|access-date=March 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320004827/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030217aaa.html|archive-date=March 20, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2017/03/10/purdue-basketball-vs-michigan-big-ten-tournament/98989456/|title=Michigan ousts Purdue from Big Ten tournament|access-date=March 19, 2017|website=Journal Courier Online|date=March 10, 2017|last=Baird|first=Nathan}}</ref>

Purdue entered the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2017 NCAA men's basketball tournament]] as the 4th seed in the Midwest bracket and played [[2016–17 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] in the first round. Purdue came away with an 80–70 win for their first tournament win in five years, with Swanigan posting a double-double with 16 points and 14 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |title=Purdue Vermont Box Score |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400946422 |access-date=April 5, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Purdue Vermont Game Summary |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=400946422 |access-date=April 5, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Purdue continued its tournament run against [[2016–17 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] in the second round. Swanigan flirted with a triple-double with 20 points, 12 rebounds and 7 assists in Purdue's 80–76 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Purdue Iowa State Game Summary |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/id/400947047 |access-date=April 5, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> In the Sweet Sixteen, Purdue squared off against [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. Swanigan was 3-for-4 from the three-point line, finishing with 18 points and seven rebounds. Purdue ended their tournament run in a loss to the Jayhawks, 98–66.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400947321|title=Purdue Kansas Box Score|publisher=ESPN|access-date=April 5, 2017}}</ref>

At the conclusion of the season, Swanigan announced he would declare for the NBA draft and not hire an agent, therefore maintaining his college eligibility for at least one more year, if necessary. Swanigan was expected to go in the late first or early second round of the NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19083185 |title=Swanigan testing draft waters again, won't hire agent yet|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|date=April 5, 2017|access-date=February 17, 2023|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Swanigan finished his academic career with a 3.60 GPA during his last semester, and maintained a cumulative GPA of 3.34.<ref name="purduedraft"/>

As a sophomore, Swanigan continued to set records at Purdue. He broke the school single-season record for rebounds, surpassing [[Joe Barry Carroll]]'s record that was set in 1979 by recording a rebound against [[2016–17 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]] in their February 21, 2017, matchup.<ref>{{cite web |last=Crespo |first=Juan |date=February 21, 2017 |title=Caleb Swanigan breaks Purdue Single Season Rebounding Record |url=http://www.hammerandrails.com/mens-basketball/2017/2/21/14692792/caleb-swanigan-breaks-purdue-single-season-rebounding-record |access-date=March 21, 2017 |website=SB Nation: Hammer and Rails}}</ref> Swanigan broke the single-season record for double-doubles at Purdue against #25 Northwestern by recording his 19th double-double.<ref>{{cite web |last=Crespo |first=Juan |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Swanigan Sets Purdue Record for Double-Doubles |url=http://www.hammerandrails.com/mens-basketball/2017/2/1/14480696/swanigan-sets-purdue-record-for-double-doubles |access-date=March 21, 2017 |website=SB Nation: Hammer and Rails}}</ref> All Big Ten players combined for the last twenty years have two 20–20 games, and Swanigan had four in a single season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Swanigan's Stats |url=https://biggie4npoy.com/his-stats/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322204109/https://biggie4npoy.com/his-stats/ |archive-date=March 22, 2017 |access-date=March 21, 2017 |website=#Biggie4NPOY }}</ref> On June 22, 2020, the [[Big Ten Network]] named Swanigan to the "All-Decade Basketball Team", placing him on their Third Team. Swanigan was one of 16 players honored by the Network for accomplishments between 2010 and 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Purdue Basketball: Caleb Swanigan & JaJuan Johnson Make All Decade Team |url=https://www.hammerandrails.com/2020/6/22/21299697/purdue-basketball-caleb-swanigan-jajuan-johnson-make-all-decade-team |website=Hammer and Rails |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=June 22, 2020 |date=June 22, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2017–2019)===
On June 22, 2017, Swanigan was drafted in the first round (26th overall) by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="nytimes_draft"/> On July 3, 2017, Swanigan signed with the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-caleb-swanigan/|title=Trail Blazers Sign Caleb Swanigan|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 3, 2017|date=July 3, 2017}}</ref> On being drafted, Swanigan said: "Being selected tonight in the NBA draft is a dream come true. I have been thinking of this moment for a long time. I know this is only the first step in my professional career, but I am extremely excited for to begin this journey." Boilermakers coach [[Matt Painter]] said, "We are thrilled that Biggie has achieved his lifelong dream of being selected in the NBA draft. It's been an incredibly tough road for him to get to this point and no one deserves it more than he does." Swanigan was the first Purdue basketball player to be drafted at the sophomore level or lower.<ref name="purduedraft">{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062217aad.html|title=Swanigan Selected 26th by Portland|access-date=July 5, 2017|publisher=Purdue|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171008035011/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062217aad.html|archive-date=October 8, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], Swanigan earned All-Summer League First Team honors for leading the Trail Blazers into the Summer League Finals, despite not winning the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/caleb-swanigan-named-all-nba-summer-league-first-team|title=CALEB SWANIGAN NAMED TO ALL-NBA SUMMER LEAGUE FIRST TEAM|publisher=NBA|access-date=June 21, 2022|date=July 17, 2017}}</ref>

Swanigan received his first [[NBA G League]] assignment, starting December 22, 2017, with the [[Canton Charge]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Trail Blazers' Caleb Swanigan: To remain with G-League team|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-caleb-swanigan-to-remain-with-g-league-team/|access-date=January 4, 2018|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=December 27, 2017}}</ref> On February 4, 2018, Portland recalled Swanigan back to the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-recall-caleb-swanigan-canton-charge|title=Trail Blazers Recall Caleb Swanigan From Canton Charge {{!}} Portland Trail Blazers|work=Portland Trail Blazers|access-date=May 31, 2018}}</ref> On December 30, he was assigned again to the G League, this time with the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS TRANSFER CALEB SWANIGAN TO NBA G LEAGUE'S TEXAS LEGENDS |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2018/12/30/blazers-transfer-caleb-swanigan-to-g-league-texas-legends |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 30, 2018 |date=December 30, 2018}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2019–2020)===
On February 7, 2019, Swanigan was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Skal Labissière]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2019/2/7/blazers-acquire-skal-labissiere|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Skal Labissière|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> He was assigned to the G League franchise the [[Stockton Kings]] on December 16.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kings' Caleb Swanigan: Sent to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/324446-kings-caleb-swanigan-sent-to-g-league/ |access-date=December 18, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 16, 2019}}</ref>

===Return to the Trail Blazers (2020)===
On January 20, 2020, Swanigan was traded back to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] along with [[Trevor Ariza]] and [[Wenyen Gabriel]] in exchange for [[Kent Bazemore]], [[Anthony Tolliver]] and two future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Trevor Ariza, Wenyen Gabriel, and Caleb Swanigan from Sacramento |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/1/20/trail-blazers-acquire-trevor-ariza-wenyen-gabriel-caleb-swanigan-from-sacramento |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 21, 2020 |date=January 20, 2020}}</ref> He opted out of playing with the Trail Blazers in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]] for personal reasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Caleb Swanigan opts out, will not join Trail Blazers for NBA restart |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/caleb-swanigan-opts-out-will-not-join-trail-blazers-nba-restart |website=NBC Sports |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=July 2, 2020 |archive-date=June 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220621212356/https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/caleb-swanigan-opts-out-will-not-join-trail-blazers-nba-restart |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Post-basketball career and death==
Following his departure from the NBA, Swanigan was charged with misdemeanor drug possession in 2021.<ref name="ArrestWANE">{{cite news |title=Update: Police found 3.4 pounds of pot in Caleb Swanigan's vehicle following traffic stop |url=https://www.wane.com/news/crime/former-homestead-and-purdue-basketball-standout-caleb-swanigan-arrested-in-whitley-county-on-drug-charges/ |access-date=27 June 2022 |work=WANE 15 |date=23 December 2020}}</ref> A photo went viral around that time which showed he had regained significant weight. The photo and [[Damian Lillard]]'s defense of Swanigan against online criticism received significant media coverage.<ref name="Washington25">{{cite news |last=Bieler |first=Des |title=Caleb Swanigan, former NBA player and Purdue star, dies at 25 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/06/21/caleb-swanigan-dies-purdue/ |access-date=June 22, 2022 |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=June 21, 2022}}</ref>

On June 20, 2022, Swanigan died in a [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]] hospital at age 25. The [[Allen County, Indiana|Allen County]] Coroner's Office reported that Swanigan "died of natural causes".<ref name="Washington25"/><ref name="ESPN25">{{cite news |title=Ex-Purdue star, NBA 1st-rounder Swanigan dies |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34125250 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |work=ESPN |date=June 21, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Norlander |first=Matt |title=Purdue All-American, former NBA player Caleb Swanigan dead at age 25 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/purdue-all-american-former-nba-player-caleb-swanigan-dead-at-age-25/ |publisher=CBSSports.com |access-date=June 22, 2022 |date=June 22, 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

===High school===
[[File:20150329 MCDAAG closed practice Caleb Swanigan (3).JPG|thumb|Swanigan driving on [[Chase Jeter]] at the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] closed practice|upright]]

Swanigan was named Indiana's Mr. Basketball and also was selected as a McDonald's All-American. He was selected as the [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] and the Indiana Basketball Coaches Association Underclass All-State first team. He was the All-USA Today Indiana Player of the year, and was selected to the Associated Press All-State Third Team.<ref name="usa"/><ref name="purdue"/>

===College===
In his freshman year, Swanigan earned the Big Ten Freshman of the week three times, a school record. He was named to the Big Ten All-Freshman Team. Swanigan was also named the National Freshman of the Week on March 8, 2016.<ref name="purdue">{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/caleb_swanigan_968091.html|title=Caleb Swanigan|website=Purdue Sports|access-date=April 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320145440/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/caleb_swanigan_968091.html|archive-date=March 20, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.purdueexponent.org/sports/article_430bb10d-2b6b-501a-8595-e4b71f15e39e.html|title=Purdue Men's Basketball: Swanigan named CBS Freshman of the Week|publisher=The Exponent|date=March 10, 2016|access-date=April 8, 2017}}</ref>

During his sophomore season, Swanigan was selected to the Preseason All-Big Ten Team. Swanigan received the Big Ten Player of the Week award six times, the second most in a season in conference history. Swanigan also was selected unanimously for the Big Ten Player of the Year in the coaches poll, the fourth in Purdue's history, and the AP Big Ten Player of the Year.<ref name="b10">{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/2016-17_All_Big_Ten_Honors.pdf|title=2016–17 All Big Ten Honors|access-date=March 19, 2017|archive-date=March 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307123951/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/2016-17_All_Big_Ten_Honors.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named the Basketball Times National Player of the Year and to five All-America teams: USBWA, Sporting News, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and NBC Sports.<ref name="p2"/> Swanigan was named the Lute Olsen National Player of the Week two times. He was also the [[Naismith Trophy]] Player of the Week and Academic All-District.<ref name="purdue"/> Swanigan was a top-four finalist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]], the player of the year award, joining [[Lonzo Ball]], [[Frank Mason III|Frank Mason]] and [[Josh Hart]]. Swanigan was also an Academic All-American for maintaining a 3.3 GPA.<ref name="p2">{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031917aaa.html|title=Swanigan Named Naismith Award Finalist|website=Purdue Sports|access-date=March 19, 2017|archive-date=March 20, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320025644/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031917aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Swanigan was a unanimous selection for first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] in both the coaches and media polls.<ref name="b10"/>
